# BFFless

> The home for your AI-generated apps, internal tools, and HTML docs — with a backend, auth, and a path to your internal services. Self-hosted, open source.

## Overview

BFFless is GitHub Pages with auth, a proxy, and a BFF. It's a self-hostable static hosting platform that wraps an immutable, SHA-keyed deploy with SSO/RBAC, a CORS-free reverse proxy to your own APIs, a no-code server-side pipeline runtime, and pluggable storage. It's where the HTML apps your AI agents produce, your internal tools, SPAs, Storybooks and docs can actually live — behind auth, inside your network. Technical framing for those who know the category: a self-hosted Supabase/Appwrite aimed at static sites and internal apps.

- Website: https://bffless.dev
- Documentation: https://docs.bffless.dev
- Full LLM Documentation: https://docs.bffless.dev/llms.txt
- App store: https://apps.bffless.dev
- Live feature demo: https://demo.bffless.dev
- Chat demo: https://chat.bffless.dev
- Video episodes: https://www.youtube.com/@bffless — searchable transcripts at https://recall.bffless.dev
- GitHub: https://github.com/bffless/ce
- License: O'Saasy (free for personal and commercial use)

Note on domains: the project moved from `bffless.app` to **`bffless.dev`**. `bffless.app` and `docs.bffless.app` redirect, but `bffless.dev` / `docs.bffless.dev` are canonical — use those.

## What is BFFless?

The static-hosting half is the easy bit — GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages or an S3 bucket will do it. The hard bit is everything between the browser and the bucket: who can see it, what it can talk to, and how it ships. BFFless is the three primitives that sit there:

1. **Self-host — your box.** One docker-compose stack (nginx, NestJS backend, React admin, PostgreSQL, SuperTokens) on a $6 droplet. Five storage adapters (S3, GCS, Azure, MinIO, local FS) swap by env var. No telemetry, no usage cap, no per-seat pricing.
2. **Auth — the missing layer.** Every deployment can sit behind SuperTokens: sessions, JWT, JWKS, Google OAuth in-box, and a pluggable seam for Okta, Azure AD or your own OIDC. Two-tier RBAC underneath; share links for one-off external review.
3. **BFF — proxy + pipelines.** Proxy rule sets per alias forward `/api/*` to any backend with no CORS fight, and a server-side pipeline runtime (form, data, email, HTTP, AI, function, file and other handlers) gives a static frontend a real backend without a Node service.

## Quick Start

Install with the script (it installs Docker if needed, configures SSL, generates secrets):

```bash
INSTALL_DIR=/opt/bffless sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://bffless.dev/install.sh)"
cd /opt/bffless && ./start.sh
```

Then open `https://admin.yourdomain.com`, finish the setup wizard, create an API key, and deploy from CI:

```yaml
- uses: bffless/upload-artifact@v1
  with:
    path: dist
    api-url: ${{ vars.BFFLESS_URL }}
    api-key: ${{ secrets.BFFLESS_API_KEY }}
    alias: production
```

That's the integration — build in CI, upload an immutable artifact keyed by commit SHA, point an alias at it. The next push doesn't replace it; it stacks beside it, and rollback is moving an alias pointer.

Setup guides: https://docs.bffless.dev/getting-started/quickstart/ · Cloudflare SSL: https://docs.bffless.dev/getting-started/cloudflare-setup/ · Let's Encrypt: https://docs.bffless.dev/getting-started/letsencrypt-setup/

## Key Features

- **Home for AI-generated apps & internal tools**: host the HTML apps, dashboards and docs your agents and teams produce, behind SSO
- **Static asset hosting**: immutable, SHA-keyed deploys uploaded from CI/CD
- **Auth & two-tier RBAC**: global roles for tenancy, per-project roles for the deploy; explicit membership, 403 otherwise
- **Proxy rules**: forward API requests to backend services without CORS; per-project defaults with per-alias overrides
- **Pipelines**: backend workflows (forms, DB records, email, outbound HTTP, custom JS) by chaining handlers — no server code
- **AI pipelines & chat**: streaming chat with OpenAI, Anthropic or Google AI, message persistence, and deployable skills
- **App catalog**: one-click install of ready-made open-source apps onto your own instance
- **Traffic splitting**: weighted A/B tests and canary rollouts with sticky sessions
- **Deployment aliases**: named pointers (production, staging, canary, `pr-123`) to specific commits
- **Custom domains**: dynamic domain mapping with automatic SSL
- **Share links**: token-scoped access to private deployments, no account needed
- **Cache rules**: per-path CDN/browser cache headers
- **Multiple storage backends**: S3, GCS, Azure Blob, MinIO, local filesystem, or S3-compatible (Spaces, R2, B2)
- **GitHub Actions**: official upload/download artifact actions

## Pipelines & Rules as Code

A pipeline is a chain of handlers bound to a route — `form_handler` → `data_create` → `email_handler` → `response_handler` is a working contact form with no server. The handler vocabulary covers data (`data_create`, `data_query`, `data_update`, `data_delete`, `data_upsert_many`, `db_aggregate`), files (`file_upload_handler`, `file_serve_handler`, `presigned_upload`, `signed_url`, `file_delete`), media (`ffmpeg_handler`, `image_convert_handler`), AI and search (`ai_handler`, `embed_store`, `vector_search`), integrations (`http_request`, `email_handler`, `github_api`, `google_calendar`, `stripe_checkout`, `stripe_webhook`, `xml_feed_parse`), and control (`function_handler`, `delay`, `response_handler`). Data lives in DB Records (schemas with typed fields, auto `id`/`createdAt`/`updatedAt`), and `{{expression}}` syntax passes values between steps (`{{input.email}}`, `{{steps.createRecord.id}}`, `{{user.email}}`).

Rule sets don't have to be clicked together in a dashboard. With the `bffless` CLI they live as YAML plus real `.fn.js` handler files under `.bffless/proxy-rules/` in your repo — diffable, testable, and reviewed in a PR:

```
.bffless/
  config.json                       # apiUrl · project · ruleSets
  proxy-rules/<set>/
    ruleset.yaml
    schemas/feedback.schema.yaml    # referenced by name, never UUID
    rules/api/feedback-form/any.rule.yaml
```

`bffless rules diff` fails a PR that has drifted from live; `bffless rules push --prune` on merge makes the server match the branch. This site's own backend is authored that way: https://github.com/bffless/bffless/tree/main/.bffless/proxy-rules

Docs: https://docs.bffless.dev/features/pipelines/ · https://docs.bffless.dev/features/ai-pipelines/ · https://docs.bffless.dev/recipes/proxy-rules-as-code/

## App Catalog

Ready-made open-source apps that install in one click from **Admin → Apps** onto your own instance — the frontend and its pipeline rule sets deploy together onto an alias you choose. Each app's backend is a reviewable rule set on your server, not someone else's. Updates are one click; every app is forkable. Requires CE ≥ 0.4.0.

| App | What it does |
|-----|--------------|
| **Handoff** | Internal file server: per-folder access control, share links for people outside the team, margin comments, and uploaded static bundles served back as live Sites |
| **Studio** | Turns a long screen recording into a short video in your own recorded voice — AI proposes the cuts, you tune them scene by scene |
| **Rivulet** | Quiet, multi-user RSS/Atom reader: folders, a river of unread items, stars, keyboard-first triage, OPML import, background refresh by scheduled pipelines |
| **Recall** | Semantic search and RAG chat over a video library — every hit deep-links to the exact second on YouTube. Live at https://recall.bffless.dev |

Browse: https://apps.bffless.dev · How installs work: https://docs.bffless.dev/features/app-catalog/

## Architecture

Every request flows through the same five layers — edge routing, auth checkpoint, pipeline runtime, BFF proxy, storage. The static artifact at the bottom is the GitHub-Pages-equivalent half; the four layers above it are the BFF server. Nothing in the request path leaves your network.

```
Internet → nginx (TLS, SPA fallback) → NestJS backend (auth · pipelines · proxy) → S3/GCS/Azure/MinIO/local
```

### Tech Stack

| Layer | Choice |
|-------|--------|
| Backend | NestJS · TypeScript |
| Frontend | React · Vite · Redux Toolkit (RTK Query) · Tailwind |
| Database | PostgreSQL · Drizzle ORM |
| Auth | SuperTokens · JWT · OAuth |
| Storage | Local · MinIO · S3 · GCS · Azure |
| Edge | nginx · TLS · Let's Encrypt or Cloudflare |
| Orchestration | Docker Compose · single host |
| Observability | Vector · TimescaleDB · Grafana (optional) |

## Security & Access Control

- Two-tier RBAC: system-wide global roles plus per-project roles; membership is explicit, and visitors without one get a 403
- API keys scoped per project for CI/CD; share links for one-off external review
- Deployments are immutable and SHA-keyed — you can't rewrite a deploy, only point an alias somewhere else, so the audit trail is free
- Proxy targets must be HTTPS; SSRF protection blocks internal IPs; header values and AI provider keys are encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM)
- Back up `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and set `COOKIE_SECURE=true` in production

Details: https://docs.bffless.dev/reference/security/

## How It Compares

| Capability | BFFless CE | GitHub Pages | Vercel · Netlify | Cloudflare Pages |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SSO / RBAC in front of the site | Yes | No | Limited | Workers code |
| Reverse proxy to any backend (no CORS) | Yes | No | Limited | Via workers |
| Custom domain + auto SSL | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Server-side pipelines (BFF, no code) | Yes | No | No | No |
| Self-host in your VPC / on-prem | Yes | Enterprise Server only | No (managed) | No (managed) |
| Immutable, SHA-keyed deploys | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Preview deployment per PR | Yes | Limited | Yes | Yes |
| Instant rollback by alias pointer | Yes | No | Rolling redeploy | Rolling redeploy |
| GitHub Action · push to deploy | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Free forever, no usage cap | Yes | Yes | Free-tier limits | Free-tier limits |

## Requirements

| Resource | Minimum | Recommended |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| RAM | 1GB | 2GB |
| Disk | 20GB | 40GB |
| CPU | 1 vCPU | 2 vCPU |

Works on any Linux server; a $5–10/month VPS from DigitalOcean, Linode or Hetzner is enough. **SSL**: Cloudflare (recommended — 15-year origin certificates, DDoS protection, CDN, no port 80) or Let's Encrypt (auto-renewing, direct connection, needs port 80).

## Use Cases

- **AI-generated apps & internal tools**: agent-produced HTML apps, dashboards and admin panels on a subdomain, behind SSO
- **Engineering docs**: Docusaurus, VitePress, MkDocs, mdBook — versioned per branch, instant rollback
- **Storybook & design systems**: publish every PR so designers and PMs can browse before merge
- **API reference sites**: Redoc, Scalar, Stoplight, hand-rolled OpenAPI HTML — gated to staff
- **CI artifacts**: coverage reports, Lighthouse runs, Playwright traces linked from the PR check
- **Runbooks & onboarding**: RBAC-gated ops content without the SaaS-of-the-month
- **Preview deployments**: every PR gets a unique URL
- **A/B tests, canary releases, feature flags**: weighted traffic splitting across aliases

## Agent Skills

`@bffless/skills` gives AI coding agents domain knowledge of BFFless — pipelines, proxy rules, rules-as-code, chat, auth, traffic splitting and more. Install with `npx skills add bffless/skills`, or as a Claude Code plugin. Source: https://github.com/bffless/skills
